name: Central bank stress
summary: Bank of England hikes to 4% on 5 Nov; ECB officials signal more tightening as euro inflation hits 4%
state: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023, as the energy shock pushes inflation up (IBTimes UK). Euro-area inflation reached 4.0% in October, a three-year high, and ECB officials signalled further hikes may be needed (Trading Economics). Policymakers face a stagflationary dilemma; no emergency or inter-meeting move had been made as of 6 Nov.
for_you: Rising policy rates feed through to mortgages, loans and savings rates over the following months. Borrowers on variable rates are most exposed.
rubric_hit: Watch: stagflationary dilemma at major central banks; no emergency move

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
